title: `worktree clear` can delete a live task both when its marker is unreadable and when a dead-owner scan races new materialisation
trigger: Five marker variants and deterministic scan/materialisation/remove test; also partial-write case.
measured: `r7-mechanisms.test.ts` showed `clearWorktrees({all:false})` removed still-live data with missing/malformed/EACCES/EIO marker (`afterCleanup:true,afterClear:false,removed:1`)
how_found_quote: `r7-mechanisms` injects a realistic write failure *after truncating the existing marker*: `ensureIsolation` rejects ENOSPC and leaves predecessor data (`survivesFailure:true`), but `clear` sees the now-empty marker and removes the live predecessor (`survivesClear:false,removed:1`).

title: separate processes sharing a workspace do not share the descendant lease
trigger: A parent with a real `ensureIsolation` generation and a second process with a live, registered `createAgentSession` at that cwd: after the owner `cleanupIsolation`
measured: the remote reported `{survives:false,disposed:false,registered:true}`, child test exited 1
how_found_quote: A parent with a real `ensureIsolation` generation and a second process with a live, registered `createAgentSession` at that cwd ... Reproduced in `r7-cross-process.test.ts`

title: same directory via symlink has different Linux lock identities
trigger: a symlink alias of the same worktree root computes a second Linux abstract-socket name; while old cleanup waited after reading the old claim, a new `ensureIsolation` through the alias wrote a new generation and live data, then old cleanup deleted it
measured: `r7-mechanisms.test.ts`: `alias lock race ... survives:false`
how_found_quote: `getLockPath` resolves `..` but not symlinks, native Linux hashes the *string* into an abstract socket; two processes can use equal directories with different lock names.

title: a non-mount rename failure falls back to an in-place teardown; if backend stop never settles it denies new materialisations
trigger: Injected EACCES, EXDEV, ENOTEMPTY ... With EBUSY rename and blocked native stop, a new `ensureIsolation`
measured: a new `ensureIsolation` instead failed `Failed to acquire lock ... after 50 attempts` (5.49s); a never-ending stop leaves no progress while process lives. Crash does *not* retain this OS lock: real holder SIGKILL then successor acquired it (and native lock suite 4/4).
how_found_quote: Crash does *not* retain this OS lock: real holder SIGKILL then successor acquired it (and native lock suite 4/4).

title: failed removal after successful rename makes a retired workspace invisible to ordinary `clear` during the live owner's whole process lifetime
trigger: Injected EIO from `fs.rm(retiredDir)`; subsequent `clearWorktrees({all:false})`
measured: `clearWorktrees({all:false})` reported `{removed:0,kept:1}`, with the old directory still present
closed_evidence: Single removal failure with a successful marker write *is fixed*, as the adapted control proves.
how_found_quote: Injected EIO from `fs.rm(retiredDir)`; subsequent `clearWorktrees({all:false})` reported `{removed:0,kept:1}`

title: first isolated sandbox on non-Linux Unix cannot acquire the file lock when the worktree root does not exist [INFERENCE]
trigger: Native non-Linux Unix `OpenOptions::open(`${baseDir}.lock`)` needs an existing parent; `ensureIsolation` acquires before its `fs.mkdir(baseDir,{recursive:true})`.
measured: This Linux host uses an abstract socket and the actual test confirms it acquires with a missing or unreadable parent (no sidecar), so no macOS run was possible here.
how_found_quote: so no macOS run was possible here

title: refusal releases before deferred disposal — OPEN for an unbounded disposal

Injecting an unresolved `flushRetainQueue` into the *real* `AgentSession.dispose` `Promise.allSettled` path, after the deadline and aborting the caller, gave `settled:false,releases:0,registered:false`; once flushed, finally cleaned up.
